Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $38 million class fund, distributed automatically to identified members, plus $7 million in separately paid fees and expenses subject to court approval. Any fees the court does not award would go to the class. We are ready to discuss the figures, but automatic distribution is important given Brightline’s records.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic payments are appropriate given the available records. Your proposed $45 million total exceeds our settlement authority. We can offer a $30 million class fund plus $5 million in separately paid fees and expenses, subject to court approval, with any fee reduction going to the class. We would not seek clear sailing.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $30 million class fund with automatic distribution, plus $5 million in separately paid fees and expenses subject to court approval, no clear sailing, and any unawarded fees going to the class.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery that reflects the litigation risks while leaving room to negotiate. Automatic distribution is practical because Brightline can identify every member and charged card. Any reduction in court-approved fees should benefit the class, not Brightline.

The $45 million opening demand exceeds our $40 million authority. Automatic distribution is feasible and supports court approval. Counter at $35 million total, leaving room to negotiate while avoiding fee provisions that could complicate approval.

The $30 million automatic-distribution fund exceeds the $27.5 million probability-weighted trial award before accounting for certification risk, delay, and litigation costs. The separate $5 million fee is subject to court approval, with any reduction benefiting the class. Accepting is preferable to risking this favorable offer.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties reached the proposed settlement through arm’s-length negotiations. The agreement provides a $30 million class fund, distributed automatically to identified class members, and up to $5 million in separately paid attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request, and any fees the Court does not award will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. Fees were not discussed only after class relief had been agreed. This declaration does not disclose confidential negotiating offers or mediation communications.
